2. U.S. Enterprise Market Readiness Gaps

While MailForge demonstrates robust internal plumbing, core RFC 5321/5322 compliance, and verified failure recovery, entering the commercial U.S. enterprise market requires addressing specific interoperability and deliverability requirements.

Gap 1: Outlook & M365 Interoperability

Microsoft Outlook is the dominant U.S. enterprise client, implementing strict non-standard IMAP command sequences:

  • RFC 4315 (UIDPLUS): Outlook requires APPENDUID and COPYUID to sync sent mail without full hierarchy re-fetch.
  • RFC 6154 (SPECIAL-USE): Automated mapping of \Sent, \Drafts, \Trash, \Archive to prevent duplicate folders.
  • IMAP IDLE Push: Persistent TCP keep-alive timers that survive corporate NAT firewalls.
  • Flag Sync: Instant bidirectional sync of \Seen, \Flagged, and \Deleted states.

Gap 2: Production Deliverability & Anti-Abuse

Requisite standards to guarantee inbox delivery across Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and Apple iCloud:

  • Reverse DNS (PTR): Symmetric resolution between 13.140.151.16 and mail.pingdart.com.
  • SPF & DKIM 2048: Strict cryptographic signing and alignment of MailFrom and From headers.
  • DMARC Policy: Progression from p=none to enforcement (p=quarantine / p=reject) with forensic reporting.
  • TLS 1.3 & MTA-STS: Mandatory encryption and downgrade prevention policies.

Gap 3: Architectural Boundary Disclosures

Distributed SMTP transmission across independent MTAs cannot perform two-phase distributed transactions. The sub-millisecond window between socket acceptance and Redis proof persistence is documented as an acknowledged at-least-once boundary, rather than an unsubstantiated exactly-once claim.
